sketches.title: Excuse Chain
sketches.premise: You and a classmate lied to a teacher about why an assignment is late. Take turns adding exactly one believable piece to the same excuse until somebody makes the whole thing collapse. Keep it plausible; make your partner look gloriously guilty.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds the next needed link without clashing with any earlier fact, while a skipped cause, a finished excuse, or an undo counts as a BREAK: the chain jumps over its needed link, ends the excuse, or takes back an established fact.
sketches.move_shape: Add one link only: a reason, then its cause, then the proof or result. Example: “The printer jammed.”
sketches.first_card: The teacher asks why your science report is three days late.

sketches.title: Paper Trail
sketches.premise: You and a classmate are forging a tiny trail of messages, notes, and receipts to support one lie told to a teacher. Build the trail one document at a time, then roast your partner by making each new scrap more awkward or risky without breaking the story.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it is the next dated or replied-to scrap that fits every document already shown; a skipped link, ending, or undo is a BREAK when it jumps past a needed message, declares the proof complete, or reverses a written fact.
sketches.move_shape: Add one new scrap with its sender, receiver, and one line of text. Example: “8:12 a.m. — Dad texts: ‘I picked you up after the dentist.’”
sketches.first_card: Your teacher wants proof that you missed class for a family errand.

sketches.title: Cover Story Ladder
sketches.premise: You and a classmate are climbing one lie from a simple answer to a painfully detailed story for a teacher. Add one rung at a time; every rung must grow from the last, while the best moves make your partner sound like a complete disaster.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds the next level of detail to the same explanation; a skipped link, ending, or undo is a BREAK when it leaps over the obvious middle, gives the final answer, or replaces an established detail.
sketches.move_shape: Add one rung that answers the next natural question. Example: “We missed the bus.” Then: “Because the dog got out.”
sketches.first_card: The teacher asks why neither of you brought the group poster.

sketches.title: Blame Baton
sketches.premise: You and a classmate are passing one shared lie back and forth while keeping it alive under a teacher’s questions. Each turn adds one handoff: what happened, who saw it, or what you did next. Pass the blame cleverly, but never snap the story in half.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it is the next believable handoff in the same account and preserves every standing fact; a skipped link, ending, or undo is a BREAK when it assigns blame without a bridge, closes the account, or cancels a fact already passed.
sketches.move_shape: Add one connected action by one person. Example: “I called you, and you said you had the poster.”
sketches.first_card: The teacher asks who was supposed to bring the missing poster.

sketches.title: Question Dodge
sketches.premise: A teacher is drilling into a lie, and you two must answer one question at a time without changing the story. Take turns adding the next answer the teacher would naturally demand; make your partner eat the worst parts while the lie stays standing.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it answers the next unanswered question using only facts already planted or one necessary new fact; a skipped link, ending, or undo is a BREAK when it dodges a needed question, gives a final wrap-up, or contradicts a prior answer.
sketches.move_shape: Add one direct answer to the next likely teacher question. Example: “At the library.”
sketches.first_card: The teacher asks why your homework has someone else’s name on it.

sketches.title: Rumor Repair
sketches.premise: Your lie to a teacher has already started spreading, and you and a classmate must keep repairing it one sentence at a time. Add the next correction or supporting detail, making your partner look suspiciously involved without creating a brand-new rumor.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it repairs or extends the same rumor in the order a listener would need, while a skipped link, ending, or undo is a BREAK when it patches over a missing cause, declares the rumor settled, or erases an accepted claim.
sketches.move_shape: Add one sentence that follows from the rumor so far. Example: “That is why the wet shoes were by the back door.”
sketches.first_card: The teacher heard that you left school before the final bell.
